ev.q: Adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) that accounted for differences in demographic characteristics were used to compare outcomes between groups.
Adolescents in the autism group were more likely to receive mental health services (41.8% versus 22.1%; aPR = 1.8, 95% CI = 1.3–2.6)
In both groups, a small percentage of adolescents (autism, 7.5%; control, 14.1%) received recommended health care transition (transition) guidance.
Adolescents in the autism group demonstrated greater difficulty carrying out daily tasks independently and had higher autism symptom severity scores
Continuous variables (e.g., mother’s and adolescent’s age, difficulty carrying out daily living tasks, and autism symptoms) were examined via linear regression.
Approximately one in five had physical difficulties, and approximately three in five had additional mental health or other conditions

methods_quotes.q: Adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) that accounted for differences in demographic characteristics were used to compare outcomes between groups.
Categorical sociodemographic variables were compared using a modified Poisson regression with robust error variance to estimate unadjusted prevalence ratios (PRs) and 95% CIs
For all other categorical variables, PRs and 95% CIs were adjusted for demographics (aPR)
